crime: She kept to the waiting places — the windows, the wall's shadow, the turn of the lake path — for hours. Girls passed without a glance.
A girl streamed every evening to a handful of watchers, greeting each by name. Half a year of evenings. Her name, not once.
That afternoon the streamer carried the broadcast out to the flower field. She was within earshot when the greeting ran once more — name by name. Hers was not among them.
When the broadcast ended she was waiting in the flowers. She took the streamer's hands; the streamer sank among the stalks, and the breath went quiet.

At the evening hour, girls found the streamer in the flower field — no wound, nothing under the nails. At a glance, a stopped heart. But faint pressure bands ringed both wrists, and the palms lay cupped open, as though someone had only just let go.
She said she had gone no farther than the wall's shadow and turned back, meeting no one. A girl from the lake path placed her past the field's edge, heading into the flowers.
The bands at the wrists were a hold, not a failing heart — the streamer died in someone's hands. She had sworn she never reached the flowers; the girl from the lake path put her there.
fields.epitaph: She kept still enough to be found by anyone who looked. No one ever looked.
fields.epithet: She Who Held Still to Be Found
execution: An iron collar closed on her throat, its chain running up through a ratchet at the beam overhead.
The chain shortened only while she was still; when she struggled, the ratchet held.
She fought it at first. Then she stopped, as she had always done, and each stillness drew the chain a few links closer.
When she was still for the last time, the ratchet drew home and she hung from the beam.

magic.name: the Becalming
magic.text: The Becalming — When she takes hold of a body, its fight drains out: clenched hands fall open, labored breath goes easy. Held long enough, the breath stops.
